title: Span and parallel-pair conditions give filtered components
statement: Use the universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be a small category such that (a) for every $a:w\to x$ and $b:w\to y$ there exist $c:x\to z$ and $d:y\to z$ with $c\circ a=d\circ b$, and (b) for every $a,b:x\to y$ there exists $c:y\to z$ with $c\circ a=c\circ b$. Then there is a small set $J$ and a partition $\operatorname{Ob}(I)=\coprod_{j\in J}S_j$ into nonempty subsets such that no morphism of $I$ joins different subsets and each full subcategory $I_j$ on $S_j$ is filtered [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Explicitly, each $I_j$ is nonempty, every two of its objects admit arrows to a common object of $I_j$, and every parallel pair of its arrows is coequalized by an arrow in $I_j$. The empty category is allowed, with $J=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Define $x\sim y$ when there exist an object $u$ and arrows $x\to u$, $y\to u$. Identities give $x\sim x$, and exchanging the two arrows proves symmetry.

For transitivity, suppose $x\to u\leftarrow y$ and $y\to v\leftarrow t$ witness $x\sim y$ and $y\sim t$. Apply hypothesis (a) to the two arrows $y\to u$ and $y\to v$, obtaining $u\to z$ and $v\to z$. Composing gives $x\to u\to z$ and $t\to v\to z$, hence $x\sim t$. Thus $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

Let $J=\operatorname{Ob}(I)/{\sim}$ and let $S_j$ be the equivalence class indexed by $j$. Each class is nonempty, distinct classes are disjoint, and their union is $\operatorname{Ob}(I)$. The quotient of the small object set and each of its classes are small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. If $I$ is empty, this construction gives $J=\varnothing$. Let $I_j$ be the full subcategory on $S_j$, with all ambient arrows between its objects and the inherited identities and composition.

For any morphism $f:x\to y$, the arrows $f$ and $\operatorname{id}_y$ witness $x\sim y$. Therefore every morphism has its endpoints in the same $S_j$, so none joins distinct classes. In particular, the full subcategories $I_j$ give the claimed disjoint decomposition.

If $x,y\in S_j$, then $x\sim y$, so choose a witness $x\to u\leftarrow y$. Since the arrow $x\to u$ implies $x\sim u$ by the preceding step, $u\in S_j$. By fullness both witness arrows lie in $I_j$. Hence every pair of objects of $I_j$ maps to a common object of $I_j$.

For parallel arrows $a,b:x\to y$ in $I_j$, hypothesis (b) supplies $c:y\to z$ with $c\circ a=c\circ b$. The arrow $c$ implies $y\sim z$, so $z\in S_j$ and fullness makes $c$ an arrow of $I_j$. Each $I_j$ is nonempty by construction; together with the preceding common-object property and this coequalization property, these are exactly the three conditions defining filteredness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].
